articleBody:
Building a home addition is a major financial and physical commitment. Before signing a contract or handing over a deposit, verify these critical items to protect your investment and avoid mid-project disputes.

- [ ] Up-to-date property survey — Confirms exact property lines, setback limits, and recorded easements to prevent boundary violations.
- [ ] Detailed architectural and structural drawings — Ensures accurate construction bidding and provides the specific blueprints necessary for local plan review.
- [ ] Active general contractor license and state registration — Proves the builder is legally qualified to pull building permits and manage residential construction.
- [ ] Proof of current general liability and workers' compensation insurance — Protects you from personal liability if property damage or jobsite injuries happen on your property.
- [ ] Clearly defined written scope of work — Spells out exact construction tasks, material selections, and site prep responsibilities so nothing is assumed.
- [ ] Clear payment milestone schedule — Links contractor payments directly to verified construction phases rather than arbitrary calendar dates.
- [ ] Formal change-order process in writing — Defines how design adjustments, hidden conditions, or price changes are documented and approved before extra work begins.
- [ ] Written permit procurement responsibility — Designates that the licensed contractor, not the homeowner, applies for, pulls, and posts all required municipal permits.

### How to Use This Checklist
Review each item alongside your contractor during the bidding and estimate review process. A qualified builder will readily supply insurance certificates, discuss permitting steps, and provide transparent written scopes without pushback.
